answer: Proposed: one subsidized key per certified chip/day; a vine of software forks gets no extra slots. Market verifiers check vendor certificates, fresh key-bound quotes of an approved kernel and chip-ID/day uniqueness; failure denies subsidy. Chips are reusable capital; rent and power recur, with no stake. 'Distinct chips imply distinct owners' is a fable: one operator can rent many. Extracted keys or dishonest vendors defeat the hardware floor. With sound chips and issuers, ten paid keys in a day need ten chips, even with shared hosts or parallel VMs.
